records.description: Thalamic visual transfer is reconstructed through paired-spike retinal efficacy and separate corticogeniculate perturbation results. Closely spaced retinal spikes differ in conditional transfer efficacy; removing layer-6 cortical input can increase or decrease dLGN responses depending on cell and contrast, while driving input reduces evoked counts in the read source. The feedback preparation uses adult GN220 Ntsr1-Cre mice during acute isoflurane-anesthetized recordings, with concentration adjusted around 1.2% using cortical LFP state. These observations distinguish retinal transmission from cortical feedback and exclude one universal positive-gain sign. They do not identify the transfer's unique cellular mechanism or jointly establish awake attention, neuromodulation, noise suppression and oscillatory routing.

studies.finding: Active albuterol improves airflow more than either placebo and no intervention; inactive comparisons are nonsignificant.
studies.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
limitations: The main scientific text, displayed Methods, Table 1 and legends of Figures 1-4 were read in PMC HTML. The separate Supplementary Appendix, trial protocol and raw spirometry/ratings were not read or replayed. Inhalers were double-blind, sham acupuncture single-blind and no intervention unblinded. The improvement-only subjective scale lacks prior formal validation and cannot represent worsening. A no-intervention study visit still includes attention, hospital context and repeated spirometry; it is not an untreated everyday natural history.
Three repeated visits per condition within one person are not three independent participants or independent studies.
A nonsignificant placebo/no-intervention difference with small reported effects does not establish exact equivalence or impossibility in every airway protocol.
Selection for bronchodilator reversibility and acute maximum-response measurement limit disease-wide and long-term generalization.

Participants are screened for at least twelve-percent reversibility to open albuterol; results do not characterize all asthma patients.

studies.finding: Selected microglial or purinergic perturbations altered neural readouts, adenosine assays and seizure susceptibility. A1 agonist rescue depended on the genetic preparation.
limitations: Adult seizure cohorts have conflicting descriptions: Animals gives 8-16 weeks for pharmacological experiments, while Seizure Induction gives 14-20 weeks for all seizure experiments. No exact age is selected from this conflict. Genetic cohorts generally include both sexes; pharmacological seizure cohorts are male.

These are distinct genetic preparations. Cx3cr1-CreERT2 targets a lineage rather than proving absolute microglia specificity; P2ry12 deletion is whole-animal, and Drd1a-Cre ligand/receptor deletions are developmental. Cre-negative littermates are the stated default controls.

Neonatal P5-P7 cultures and adult in vivo preparations remain separate. Figure 4c is extracellular striatal dialysate under isoflurane; Figure 4h is a tissue-homogenate fluorescence assay after D1 agonist.

Cortical bouton imaging and striatal calcium imaging are different preparations. The cortical caption says intraperitoneal CNO/clopidogrel while its Methods says intravenous CNO. The neuronal-imaging virus volume and the A1-antagonist dose units also contain unresolved inconsistencies.

Cell and process counts do not replace independent mice. Calcium magnitude and rate-interaction nulls, receptor-specific rescue failures and challenge-specific nulls constrain generalization. Code, raw imaging and all supplementary datasets have not been independently replayed.

Published results and source-table checks are not an independent biological replication. Behavioral stage IV-V seizures are an induced challenge endpoint, not a universal measure of neural stability or a human treatment result.
